### 1. Architecture Overview

Prometheus’s **native histogram model** (defined in `model/histogram/histogram.go`) is the canonical sparse histogram representation used end-to-end by the TSDB, text parser, and remote‑write stack. Clients such as `promtool`/`prometheus` ingest histogram samples via the text-parsing layer (`model/textparse/*`) and materialize them as `histogram.Histogram` instances (see iterator and validation helpers at `model/histogram/histogram.go`). NHCB conversion in `util/convertnhcb/convertnhcb.go` builds `*histogram.Histogram`/`*histogram.FloatHistogram` representations that are streamed downstream for storage or remote-write compatibility, while the text parser wrapper `model/textparse/nhcbparse.go` collates classic histogram buckets into those `Histogram` instances before emitting them through the parser interface (Sections “Collation Pattern” and “Conversion Validation” in `nhcbparse.go`). The histogram type is subsequently consumed by storage (TSDB chunks, record encoding, `promql` iterators) and remote write codecs (`prompb/*`); any literal instantiation therefore needs to remain in sync with this shared model.

Adding a **required `CreatedTimestamp int64` field** to `Histogram` means every literal construction (tests, helpers, conversion code, NHCB parser buffers) must be updated so the new field is populated, or else Go’s struct literal rules will break compilation for every file that initializes `Histogram{…}` (e.g., `Histogram{Schema: …}` in `model/histogram/histogram_test.go` and countless other call sites). Because the struct spans parsing, conversion, TSDB serialization, and PromQL evaluation, the change must propagate through the text parser (`nhcbparse.go`), converter utilities (`convert.go`, `convertnhcb`), and any tests or helpers that form `Histogram` values.

### 2. Detailed Analysis

#### Histogram Core Definition
- `model/histogram/histogram.go` defines the `Histogram` struct and its methods (Copy, Validate, iterators) for sparse positive/negative buckets, spans, sum, count, and custom buckets (“Type definitions for CounterResetHint, Histogram, and Span” and sections `Copy`, `Validate`, iterators, `ReduceResolution`). Adding a `CreatedTimestamp int64` field alters the struct layout, so every code path that constructs a histogram literal, copies or compares histograms, or serializes/deserializes will now need to supply/handle the timestamp (see sections “Sparse Histogram Representation” and “Validation Logic”) (model/histogram/histogram.go).

#### Literal Construction Sites and Tests
- `model/histogram/histogram_test.go` directly instantiates numerous `Histogram` literals (e.g., `Histogram{Schema: 0, Count: 19, Sum: 2.7, PositiveSpans: …}` in multiple test cases such as `TestHistogramString`, `TestCumulativeBucketIterator`, `TestRegularBucketIterator`, `TestHistogramToFloat`)—each literal will fail to compile unless `CreatedTimestamp` is set or omitted via non-literal construction (all rooted in the `cases` tables shown at the top of `histogram_test.go`). This file alone proves that there are many explicit struct literal constructions.

- `model/histogram/generic_test.go` also touches histogram primitives used by resolution reduction helpers, and though it focuses on spans/buckets, any helper that assembles a `Histogram` for `mustReduceResolution` will indirectly require the new field to be assigned if a literal is used (see `TestReduceResolutionHistogram` and `TestReduceResolutionFloatHistogram`).

- `model/histogram/float_histogram_test.go` contains additional histogram literal creation for comparative testing between `Histogram` and `FloatHistogram` (“TestFloatHistogramMul”, “TestFloatHistogramCopy”, etc.). When the `Histogram` struct shape changes, tests comparing float histograms to `Histogram` instances may fail unless they mirror the new field.

#### Conversion & Parser Layers
- `model/histogram/convert.go` converts a native histogram (NHCB) back to classic histogram series; it accepts `*Histogram` and simply assumes the fields defined in `Histogram`. If `CreatedTimestamp` is mandatory, this conversion pipeline must either set the new field (e.g., when populating a new `Histogram`) or propagate it through the validation/emit stages (see the `ConvertNHCBToClassic` function and its switch on `*Histogram`/`*FloatHistogram`).

- `model/textparse/nhcbparse.go` collates classic histogram series and eventually caches `*histogram.Histogram`/`*histogram.FloatHistogram` instances (`processNHCB`, `handleClassicHistogramSeries`, etc.). The parser’s state machine will either need to track `CreatedTimestamp` when `p.tempNHCB.Convert()` returns a `*Histogram` or ensure the conversion utilities it relies on already set the field before the histogram is stored/emitted (“Collation Pattern” and “Conversion Validation” in sections around lines 277‑397).

- `model/textparse/nhcbparse_test.go` constructs expected entries and validates parser output, indirectly relying on `Histogram` semantics (see summary sections “TestNHCBParserOnOMParser” and “TestNHCBParserResetLastExponential”). If the parser now populates `CreatedTimestamp`, tests should assert the correct value; otherwise, they may fail to compare histograms that newly report the field.

- `util/convertnhcb/convertnhcb.go` (purpose: “incrementally collect and convert classic histogram samples into histogram.Histogram/FloatHistogram”) is the production code path responsible for building `Histogram` literals or zero-valued structures. A new `CreatedTimestamp` field will probably need to be added to the temporary histogram state and propagated onto the converted `Histogram`.

#### Broader Impact (Downstream Consumers)
- Any TSDB or remote-storage code that uses literal initialization or default-zero semantics must now account for `CreatedTimestamp`. For instance, `prompb/codec.go` and `prompb/io/prometheus/write/v2/codec.go` convert `Histogram` values to/from protobuf; they will now either read/write the new field or rely on the `CreatedTimestamp` being defaulted by the histogram constructors called upstream (and those constructors must therefore set it accurately).

- PromQL iterators (`promql/histogram_stats_iterator.go`) and JSON parsing layers (`model/textparse/*`) that rely on the `Histogram` shape must also remain aligned; any literal expectations there (e.g., zero-valued `Histogram` used for initialization) will require minimal updates but should be reviewed.

### 3. Relevant Files

| Repo       | File Path | Why |
|------------|-----------|-----|
| prometheus | model/histogram/histogram.go | Defines the `Histogram` struct (Copy, Validate, iterators) referenced by NHCB parser, TSDB, converters; new `CreatedTimestamp` field changes the struct shape and thus all constructors. |
| prometheus | model/histogram/convert.go | `ConvertNHCBToClassic` accepts `*Histogram` and `*FloatHistogram`; must propagate the new field when converting back to legacy series. |
| prometheus | model/histogram/histogram_test.go | Instantiates dozens of `Histogram{…}` literals (see `TestHistogramString`, iterators, conversions); each literal must be updated to supply or tolerate `CreatedTimestamp`. |
| prometheus | model/histogram/generic_test.go | Builds histograms and spans for resolution reduction tests; any histogram literal there depends on the struct definition. |
| prometheus | model/histogram/float_histogram_test.go | Contains constructors of `Histogram`/`FloatHistogram` values in tests (multiplication, copy, division), so the test scaffolding must set `CreatedTimestamp` as well. |
| prometheus | model/textparse/nhcbparse.go | Collates classic histogram series into `*histogram.Histogram` and stores them (`processNHCB`, `handleClassicHistogramSeries`); will need to set `CreatedTimestamp` on converted histograms emitted by the parser. |
| prometheus | model/textparse/nhcbparse_test.go | Validates NHCB parser output; any histogram fields compared against expected values must include the new timestamp, or tests will fail. |
| prometheus | util/convertnhcb/convertnhcb.go | Creates NHCB `Histogram`/`FloatHistogram` instances; must initialize `CreatedTimestamp` before returning the converted histogram. |
| prometheus | prompb/codec.go | Serializes/deserializes `Histogram` to remote-write protos (imports `model/histogram`); must be kept consistent with the new field. |
| prometheus | prompb/io/prometheus/write/v2/codec.go | Remote-write v2 codec that handles histogram fields; needs to read/write `CreatedTimestamp` if it becomes part of the protobuf contract (otherwise it must ignore but ensure defaults). |
| prometheus | promql/histogram_stats_iterator.go | Consumes histogram samples and iterators; if the iterator yields literal `Histogram` values, their new field must be set/propagated. |
| prometheus | tsdb/record/record.go | Encodes/decodes TSDB WAL snapshots—including histograms—so the stored struct must stay in sync. |
| prometheus | tsdb/head_append_v2.go | `AppenderV2` implementations append histogram samples; they will build `Histogram` values and must continue to compile with the new field. |
| prometheus | tsdb/chunkenc/chunk.go | TSDB chunk encodings for histograms rely on `Histogram` structure shape; ensure constructors and zero values include `CreatedTimestamp`. |
| prometheus | tsdb/chunks/samples.go | Defines sample data structures that wrap `Histogram`; new field must be maintained when samples are created. |
| prometheus | storage/buffer.go | Stores recent samples (including histograms) in a buffer; any struct initialization needs to account for `CreatedTimestamp`. |
| prometheus | cmd/prometheus/main.go | Imports `model/histogram` (via storage stack) and interacts through the TSDB; while not instantiating `Histogram` directly, it relies on downstream histograms, so builders/upstream code must set the new field. |
| prometheus | cmd/promtool/unittest.go | Uses histogram structures when evaluating rule tests; the embedded histograms must respect the new field to keep tests valid. |

> **Note:** The above list covers every file discovered during the audit that either defines, constructs, converts, compares, or parses `histogram.Histogram`. They must all be reviewed to ensure the new `CreatedTimestamp int64` field is set wherever a literal or converted histogram is created, so downstream consumers (NHCB parser, TSDB, remote-write codecs, tests) continue to build and validate the native histogram representation correctly.

SUMMARY: Adding a required CreatedTimestamp int64 field to the Histogram struct in prometheus/model/histogram/histogram.go will break all existing literal constructions of Histogram across the codebase. Every file that instantiates Histogram values—such as tests, conversion utilities, the NHCB parser, and storage/remote-write codecs—must be updated to supply the new field or use non-literal construction to avoid compilation errors.

FILES:
- prometheus/model/histogram/histogram.go — Defines the Histogram struct; adding the new field changes its shape and affects all downstream usage.
- prometheus/model/histogram/histogram_test.go — Contains many Histogram literal constructions that will fail to compile without the new field.
- prometheus/model/histogram/generic_test.go — Builds Histogram values for resolution reduction tests; literals must be updated.
- prometheus/model/histogram/float_histogram_test.go — Instantiates Histogram literals in comparative tests; requires the new field.
- prometheus/model/histogram/convert.go — Converts Histogram to classic series; must propagate CreatedTimestamp when creating or handling Histogram values.
- prometheus/model/textparse/nhcbparse.go — Collates classic histograms into Histogram instances; must set CreatedTimestamp on converted histograms.
- prometheus/model/textparse/nhcbparse_test.go — Validates parser output; expected Histogram values must include CreatedTimestamp.
- prometheus/util/convertnhcb/convertnhcb.go — Produces Histogram instances from NHCB; must initialize CreatedTimestamp.
- prometheus/prompb/codec.go — Serializes/deserializes Histogram for remote write; must handle the new field.
- prometheus/prompb/io/prometheus/write/v2/codec.go — Remote-write v2 codec; must read/write CreatedTimestamp if part of the protobuf contract.
- prometheus/promql/histogram_stats_iterator.go — Consumes Histogram samples; must propagate CreatedTimestamp if constructing literals.
- prometheus/tsdb/record/record.go — Encodes/decodes Histogram in WAL; must stay in sync with struct changes.
- prometheus/tsdb/head_append_v2.go — Appends Histogram samples; must compile with the new field when constructing Histogram values.
- prometheus/tsdb/chunkenc/chunk.go — TSDB chunk encoding for Histogram; relies on struct shape and constructors.
- prometheus/tsdb/chunks/samples.go — Wraps Histogram in sample structures; must account for CreatedTimestamp.
- prometheus/storage/buffer.go — Buffers samples including Histogram; any literal initialization must include the new field.
- prometheus/cmd/prometheus/main.go — Uses histogram via storage stack; upstream code must set CreatedTimestamp.
- prometheus/cmd/promtool/unittest.go — Evaluates rules with Histogram; embedded histograms must include CreatedTimestamp.
